combat.answer: Wither skulls explode on impact and can apply Wither. The slower blue skull has stronger block-breaking properties than an ordinary black skull.

health.answer: Wild Bedrock wolves have 8 health points (4 hearts); tamed wolves have 40 health points (20 hearts).

spawning.answer: Wolf variants live in different biomes: pale in taiga; woods in forest; ashen in snowy taiga; black in old growth pine taiga; chestnut in old growth spruce taiga; rusty in sparse jungle; spotted in savanna plateau; striped in wooded badlands; snowy in grove.

variants.answer: There are nine wolf variants: pale, woods, ashen, black, chestnut, rusty, spotted, striped and snowy. Their home biomes differ. A baby inherits a parent’s variant rather than changing to match the breeding biome.

drops.answer: Wolves have no ordinary meat or fur drop. Equipped wolf armor drops separately. Experience depends on age and the kill conditions.

taming.answer: Feed bones to a wild, non-angry wolf. Each bone has a one-in-three chance to tame it. A wolf already owned by another player cannot be tamed again.

breeding.answer: Feed meat to two standing, tamed adult wolves at full health. Rotten flesh and raw chicken work. Bedrock has a one-minute breeding cooldown; do not use Java-only fish breeding rules.

interactions.answer: Tamed wolves follow their owner or can sit. Meat heals them, dyes change their collars, and wolf armor provides protection.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Look for pale wolves in the taiga biome.
Look for woods wolves in the forest biome.
Look for ashen wolves in the snowy taiga biome.
Look for black wolves in the old growth pine taiga biome.
Look for chestnut wolves in the old growth spruce taiga biome.
Look for rusty wolves in the sparse jungle biome.
Look for spotted wolves in the savanna plateau biome.
Look for striped wolves in the wooded badlands biome.
Look for snowy wolves in the grove biome.
Throw a bottle o’ enchanting or dispense it to create the projectile.

interactions.answer: The bottle breaks on impact and releases experience orbs. It does not directly apply an enchantment to an item.

spawning.answer: Experience orbs come from activities such as suitable mob kills, mining certain ores, smelting, breeding and trading.

interactions.answer: Nearby experience orbs move toward players and are collected for experience. Mending can use collected experience to repair eligible equipment.

health.answer: Zoglins have 40 health points (20 hearts).

spawning.answer: A hoglin outside the Nether becomes a zoglin after about 15 seconds.

drops.answer: Zoglins can drop 1–3 rotten flesh, including babies, with applicable Looting increases.

breeding.answer: Zoglins cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Zoglins cannot be tamed.

combat.answer: Zoglins attack many nearby creatures, including players. Do not treat one as a living hoglin that can be controlled with fungi.

health.answer: Bedrock zombies have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombies appear in suitable dark Overworld areas and from monster or trial spawners. Deserts often produce husks instead.

drops.answer: Zombies can drop 0–2 rotten flesh, with rare iron ingot, carrot or potato drops under player-kill conditions. Equipment has separate rules. A charged-creeper kill can produce a zombie head.

interactions.answer: Zombies burn in daylight unless protected. They can infect villagers: the conversion chance is 0% on Easy, 50% on Normal and 100% on Hard. A submerged zombie can become a drowned.

health.answer: Zombie horses have 25 health points.

spawning.answer: Zombie horsemen can appear at night or during thunderstorms in suitable plains and savanna biomes and snowy plains; Bedrock also includes ice spikes. The mounted zombie is a separate entity.

drops.answer: Zombie horses can drop 2–3 rotten flesh plus applicable equipped items. The rider has separate loot.

taming.answer: Repeatedly ride a zombie horse until it accepts you, then use suitable equipment to control it.

breeding.answer: Zombie horses cannot be bred.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

health.answer: Zombie nautiluses have 15 health points.

spawning.answer: Some trident-wielding drowned can spawn riding zombie nautiluses outside rivers and frozen rivers. Warm-ocean spawning can produce the coral variant.

drops.answer: Zombie nautiluses can drop rotten flesh and applicable equipped items. A drowned rider has its own separate loot.

taming.answer: Feed pufferfish or a bucket of pufferfish to a zombie nautilus. Each feeding has a one-in-three taming chance.

variants.answer: Zombie nautiluses have ordinary and coral forms; the coral form is associated with warm oceans.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

health.answer: Bedrock zombified piglins have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombified piglins appear in suitable Nether areas, near active Overworld Nether portals, from pigs struck by lightning, or when piglins remain outside the Nether.

drops.answer: They can drop rotten flesh and gold nuggets, with rare gold ingots under player-kill conditions. Equipped weapons have separate chances.

interactions.answer: Zombified piglins are usually neutral until provoked, then nearby members can become angry. They do not barter with gold and cannot be cured back into piglins.

health.answer: Bedrock zombie villagers have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombie villagers can spawn with zombies, generate in abandoned villages and igloo basements, or result from villagers being killed by zombies. Infection depends on difficulty.

drops.answer: Zombie villagers can drop rotten flesh, rare iron ingots, carrots or potatoes, and applicable equipment under their own loot conditions.

interactions.answer: Apply Weakness, then feed a normal golden apple to start curing a zombie villager. Protect it while it converts. An enchanted golden apple is not the curing ingredient.
